newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour steps up attack on Conservatives.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour steps up attack on Conservatives.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour Party on Thursday stepped up its attack on the ruling Conservatives by ordering that the party's 10-point programme be delivered to every household in the country.
Labour leader Tony Blair told a news conference that he was determined that what he called the positive tone of Labour's campaign should drown out Prime Minister John Major's negative message.
"Today (deputy Labour leader) John Prescott and I have issued instructions that the Contract must be got into every home in the country," Blair said.

"The Tory Lie Machine is now moving up a gear, so it is vital that we move up a gear in our positive campaigning. The contract is the key to that. The truth is the Tories are running for office, but running away from their record."
Labour's manifesto, launched last week, is based on a 10-point contract with the British people' in which Labour commits itself to a core list of promises.
Blair, again making trust the campaign theme of the day, accused Major's Conservatives of repeatedly breaking promises over the past five years, particularly on tax.

The Labour leader challenged Major to confirm the conclusion of the Institute of Fiscal Studies that taxes have risen since the 1992 election and thst the average family is at least seven pounds ($11.36) a week worse off.
